summary: Interpreted the first sweep receipt whose liveness counters are interpretable (CheckRun 0e5183701ac3447c8398f246b9103a04: completed, tests_passed, exit 0, 17 parsed observations, 0 parse errors). Indices 0-15 reproduce probes A-C; index 16 reports seeds=60, steps_per_seed=60, elections=470, ordinary proposals=461, conf_change_proposals=262, restarts=429, unapplied_conf_change_states=48, stalled_states=0, violations=0, and no liveness_witness event because the witness never fired. Since application lag was introduced (a randomly chosen node skips its apply step about one time in six), the antecedent now holds at 48 of 3600 check points, so the zero is informative for this event set: in every one of those 48 states at least one node remained promotable, meaning the campaign suppression never coincided with a configuration that had no candidate able to campaign - a real, if descriptive, answer to the bounded-liveness side of the guard. The safety half is unchanged and now carries lag too: no witness for at-most-one-leader-per-term, committed (index, term) consistency, committed-index monotonicity or applied <= committed across 262 configuration changes (half joint with the target's own auto-leave), 429 restarts rebuilt from persisted state, and ordinary traffic. I updated the gap answer to reflect the receipts now covering configuration changes, joint transitions, a real joining participant, restarts and application lag, while deliberately leaving it unresolved: 48 antecedent observations over one fixed seed set bound nothing outside it, the witness checks that some node is promotable rather than that a quorum of voters can campaign, lag was one-step and never combined with a partition of the lagging node, demotion of an existing serving voter remains absent from the event set, and checks still happen between events with term-level rather than full-identity comparison of committed entries.
